text.en: A baby under 6 months who is feeding poorly or not waking for feeds should go to hospital immediately, without waiting for complete refusal; this is the Australian Royal Children’s Hospital advice. UK NHS advice is to call emergency services or go to emergency care when a child under 5 is not feeding, not responding normally, sleepier than usual or difficult to wake.

text.en: Outside the infant and emergency situations above, a child drinking less, struggling to replace fluids after vomiting, or having fewer wet nappies/less urine needs prompt pediatric or local urgent medical advice. Marked lethargy, rapid deterioration or any of the warning signs above requires emergency assessment.
